args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also marked unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. A human approver signed off on the rollback. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to deploy it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** after v2.3.1 was deployed, all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. An approver signed off before the rollback ran. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 covers the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again.

v2.3.1 reached production even though its test version (v2.3.1-rc) was already marked unhealthy in staging. It's worth finding out why that didn't stop the release.
